key_insight: A neural-hierarchical robotic skin combines densely packed iontronic sensors with fast readout and data compression. It enables humanoid robots to sense fine textures, handle delicate objects and respond to potentially damaging stimuli.
problem_solved: Large-area robotic skin must capture detailed touch information while efficiently reading and processing signals from many sensors.
method: Use a high-density iontronic sensor array to capture detailed tactile signals.
Combine fast sensor readout with data compression in a neural-hierarchical processing architecture.
Enable tactile capabilities including texture perception, delicate-object manipulation and responses to nociceptive stimuli.
impact: For robotics and embodied AI practitioners, this work highlights a hardware–processing approach for making rich tactile sensing more manageable at scale. Such sensing could support more responsive and careful physical interaction.
visual_elements: Layered schematic showing robotic skin, the iontronic sensor array and hierarchical processing.

paper_title: Large-scale iontronic skins with neural-hierarchical processing architecture
paper_authors: Zhibin Li, Bingxu Da, Junli Shi, Taihong Wang, Wenlong Si
